result.summary:
The data and runtime side of individual cities is done and committed as 10ed099 on worktree-wf_aa93e7ca-cf8-1. The full suite passes: 292 unit tests and all integration checks. Everything works with fallback sprites now. No Blender asset exists yet.

**Data**
- `data/cities.json` covers all 45 cities. Each has a building style (16 styles), landmarks with real heights, background silhouettes and bridges.
- Hamburg arrives over a cable-stayed bridge (Köhlbrandbrücke) and a truss-arch bridge (Elbbrücken). Amsterdam has five canal bridges with houseboats, Venice the causeway over the lagoon, Kiel a high bridge over the canal.
- Paris, Prague, Dresden, Budapest, Vienna, Bordeaux, Lyon, Belgrade, Riga, Warsaw and others get river bridges.
- A new pure class `CityData` resolves this for the destination city. It drops bridges that hit a tunnel or leave the stage, and landmarks outside the City Limits, in a tunnel or in the water, with a warning.
- `data/scenery.json` has an outskirts and a centre scenery for each of the 16 styles (32 entries). They use 53 new building ids `props/city_<stil>_<name>`, each with a fallback sprite and a fallback-only tint. Each style has its own ground colour, background and, in the outskirts, fences or hedges. Eastern outskirts get small houses with picket fences and gardens, as the user asked.

**Runtime**
- The track switches from outskirts to centre scenery 8 km before the finish (per city adjustable).
- Landmarks are placed as events with a cleared plaza on their side and a few park trees.
- Bridges are zones: water beside and under the deck, quay walls or grassy embankments at the banks, and no scenery on the water. Truss bridges get an overhead portal every 40 m. Cable-stayed bridges get pylons with 3D stay cables, stone bridges and the causeway get ornate lamps.
- The renderer draws the water with sky reflection and glints, darker at night with shimmering city lights. Each bridge type has its own railing.
- Landmarks stay visible well beyond the normal draw distance and fade in with the haze, so they don't pop in.
- Ten landmarks have procedural stand-ins until their sprites exist, including the Eiffel tower (golden at night), the Berlin TV tower, the Riesenrad, the Campanile, the Budapest parliament and the Warsaw Palace of Culture.
- Skyline landmarks appear as hazy silhouettes in the background panorama and turn with it. A silhouette fades out once the same landmark is in view as a prop, so it never shows twice.
- The race session shows the bridge name in the HUD.

**Checks**
- Every arrival in every city (both directions of all stages) builds without warnings.
- Frame time in city sections: 4.3–5.5 ms minimum against 4.8 ms outside the city, measured on a busy machine (load about 7).

**Screenshots**
All in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/final/`. The labelled overview is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/final/uebersicht.png`. It covers Paris, the Hamburg bridge entry, the Amsterdam canals, Vienna, Białystok's outskirts, Venice, Kiel and Kassel.
deviations: Bridge length_m is read as visible metres, the project's convention for every *_m value (1 km on the odometer = 83.3 m). With that, the example values in contract §1 for Hamburg don't fit: 700 m would be 8.4 km and overlap the second bridge. Also the Elbtunnel lies 7.3–4.0 km before the finish when arriving from Hannover. Hamburg is therefore: Köhlbrandbrücke at 17.0 km / 260 m, Elbbrücken at 11.0 km / 200 m, Elbphilharmonie at 3.4 km, Michel at 1.8 km. Documented in staedte.md §6.

I added data fields beyond the contract. Bridges: name, height_m, water, color, bank, ships, boats, pylon_m. Landmarks: name, tint, clear_m, plaza, and plain existing props as landmarks (props/church with scale and tint). Also a landmark catalogue `landmark_sets` (height, width, required, proc, fallback), center_km per city, skyline entries as objects, per-city background overrides, and scenery keys fence, water, fallback_tint, suburb, roofs, behind and five new skyline features.

The single vertical bank wall became a profile under the deck (TrackSegment.water_level): one-segment quay walls in cities, long grassy embankments for high bridges. The high bridges in Kiel and Bern use 15–16 m of water depth instead of the real ~40 m, otherwise the deck hides the water.

Lights of landmarks and lamp reflections on water are drawn as soft spots in normal depth order, not in the additive glow layer. The glow layer is drawn last, so it shone through hills and through the bridge deck.
Procedural stay cables are only drawn with the procedural pylon. The contract says the bridge_pylon sprite carries its own cable fan.

The optional settings render.landmark_far_m (1900), render.landmark_range_factor (2.0) and render.skyline_distance_m (1800) are defaults in code. I did not add them to config/game_config.json, to avoid merge conflicts with the other agents. They are documented as optional.
No city uses the `austrian` style (Wien uses `vienna`). It is still complete as the default for Austria.
notes_for_lead: Assets still missing (everything runs on fallbacks): all 53 building ids listed in docs/staedte.md §8 'Gebäudeliste'; the four bridge parts props/bridge_truss_arch, props/bridge_pylon, props/bridge_lamp, props/houseboat; and all 26 landmarks. Of the landmarks, 15 are required: landmarks/eiffel_tower, elbphilharmonie, michel, riesenrad, stephansdom, fernsehturm_berlin, frauenkirche_dresden, frauenkirche_muenchen, sagrada_familia, duomo_milano, campanile_venezia, parlament_budapest, veitsdom_prag, kulturpalast_warschau, nevsky_kathedrale. Five are 'by time' (frankfurter_hochhaeuser, kaiserburg_nuernberg, freiheitsdenkmal_riga, kathedrale_burgos, basilica_pilar) and six optional (florianturm, fernsehturm_riga, cuatro_torres, sacre_coeur, hram_svetog_save, herkules_kassel).

The ids in docs/staedte.md §8 are the names data/scenery.json and data/cities.json reference. If the Blender agent picked different names, rename them in the data, not in code. A sprite that exists under the old name simply won't be used. CityData.validate()/missing_props() only report ids that have neither a sprite nor a fallback.

Requirements for the sprites, per docs/staedte.md §8. Landmarks: no mirror_left, anchor on the ground, extent_m set (they are placed with align edge), real size, lights layer used as floodlighting. bridge_truss_arch: front view, anchor bottom centre, object.width_m is used to scale it to the deck width, clear height at least 6 m. houseboat: anchor at the middle of the waterline. Buildings: same conventions as props/building_* (3/4 view for the right roadside, mirror_left, extent_m).

My changes to scripts/race/race_session.gd are small: the scenery line in the view, a `_was_bridge` variable and the bridge-name message in `_check_zones`. They may conflict on merge with the audio or driving-physics agents.
The 'ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' warning in screenshot runs is an AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback from the audio module. It is unrelated to the city work.

The generator scripts I used for the data are in the scratchpad, not the repo: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/gen_cities.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/gen_scenery.py. The JSON files are now the source of truth and hand edits are fine.

To reproduce the screenshots: tools/screenshot.sh <prefix> --stage=kiel_hamburg --start-km=83.6 --start-speed=60 --hour=12 --autopilot --no-countdown --shot-times=1.5. Other positions are listed in docs/staedte.md §9. Overview image: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/final/uebersicht.png.

result.summary:
All 15 must-have landmark sprites and 6 of the optional ones are rendered at full quality and committed on my branch (21 sets, ids landmarks/<name>). The validator passes with 0 errors and 2 warnings, and tools/run_tests.sh passes (126 scripts, 273 tests, 0 failures, integration checks OK).

- **Must-have:** eiffel_tower, elbphilharmonie, michel, riesenrad, stephansdom, fernsehturm_berlin, frauenkirche_dresden, frauenkirche_muenchen, sagrada_familia (2026 state, 172.5 m with the cross), duomo_milano, campanile_venezia (with the San Marco domes), parlament_budapest, veitsdom_prag (with the castle front), kulturpalast_warschau, nevsky_kathedrale.
- **Optional:** frankfurt_skyline, kaiserburg_nuernberg, st_petri_riga, freiheitsdenkmal_riga, kathedrale_burgos, basilica_pilar.

Built procedurally in the new module tools/blender/cesprites/props_landmarks.py, reusing the existing rig, materials and light passes. Real heights and footprints, checked against web sources where I was unsure.
- **Sprite properties:** each set has one angle "c" (a 3/4 view, camera 3° from level), layers base and lights, the anchor on the ground at the centre of the near face, real width/length/height in "object", tags prop and landmark, and no mirror_left.
- **Night look:** floodlit facades from a noise-free version of the base colour (keeps the light layers small), lit windows, red aviation lights, the golden Eiffel tower, the Sagrada cross and star, the Riesenrad bulbs.
- **Cell sizes:** 2–6.4 px/m, at most 1024 px high and 960 px wide, so close to 1:1 when passing at 150–300 m.
- **Import:** lossless with mipmaps, like the other props; the .import files are committed.
- **Size:** 6.1 MB PNG, render time 7.5 min with 2 threads.

Visual checks before committing:
- Day/night previews and the contact sheet, plus a lineup of all landmarks at the same scale.
- A simulated in-game view of every landmark at day and night, at far distance and at 260 m, on real game screenshots.
- Real in-game runs using SpriteDB's debug overlay with aliases (wind turbines and farmhouses shown as landmarks): the Eiffel tower and Elbphilharmonie with quick renders, then the TV tower and Sagrada with the committed assets. All load and draw correctly at day and night.
files_changed: assets/sprites/manifest.json (21 landmark entries added, nothing removed)
deviations: Render caching: render_all.CODE['landmark'] does not hash props_landmarks.py. Instead each landmark set carries params['rev'], a hash of the module's shared code plus its own builder, so editing one landmark re-renders only that one. Documented in the code and in docs/sprites.md.
frankfurt_skyline puts six real towers closer together into one skyline group (about 320 m wide). It is not a single building.

The validator gives 2 warnings (not errors): the very wide eiffel_tower and parlament_budapest reach 1.2–1.7 m below the anchor line, because their near corner comes forward in the 3/4 view. This is harmless at these scales and documented.

Wikipedia was not reachable from the session (de.wikipedia.org would have to be allowed); I used web search instead. Three colour choices could not be confirmed: the Riesenrad steel (dark red-brown), the attic cube of the Campanile (light stone) and the Prague castle roofs (green copper).
notes_for_lead: PNG budget: the repo is now at 58.5 of 60 MB, with the landmarks at 6.1 MB. Merging this with the parallel city-building sprites will very likely go over the validator's 60 MB limit (validate_manifest --max-mb). Either raise the budget (the GPU load per stage is only the 1–3 landmarks of the target city) or make the buildings very small.
For the runtime/data agents: the landmarks are never mirrored and show the same view on either side of the road. extent_m works like for all other props. They are tagged prop and landmark.

Placement: very tall landmarks get cut off at the top when close. The Eiffel tower (330 m) and TV tower (368 m) only fit on screen from about 700 m depth. Beyond the 900 m draw distance the normal fog fades them out, so the planned early fade-in for landmarks matters.
GPU memory is 56 MB if all landmarks are loaded, but only 2–9 MB for the 1–3 landmarks of one stage.

Edits to shared files are small and additive: catalog.py (the all_sets return line plus a landmark_sets() helper), render_all.py (one CODE entry plus a build branch), validate_manifest.py (LANDMARKS list, checks, docstring), contact_sheet.py (landmarks category plus lineup_landmarks.png). Most likely merge conflicts: the docs/sprites.md section placed before 'Renderzeiten' and the table row after 'UI'.

The optional ids (frankfurt_skyline, kaiserburg_nuernberg, st_petri_riga, freiheitsdenkmal_riga, kathedrale_burgos, basilica_pilar) are listed in docs/staedte.md §3 so data/cities.json can use them. The validator only requires the 15 must-haves.

Verification images are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/landmarks/: f1.png–f4.png (final day/night previews), final/contact_landmarks.png and final/lineup_landmarks.png, simp_*.png and simc_*.png (simulated in-game views), game_*.png (real in-game screenshots), plus the tools preview.py, ingame_sim.py and make_overlay.py.

result.summary:
Built the regional city buildings (contract §2) and the bridge parts (§4) procedurally in Blender. They live in the new module tools/blender/cesprites/props_cities.py and are rendered at final quality into assets/sprites: 50 sets in total.

- 46 buildings, ids props/city_<style>_<name>, across 15 styles. The eastern style has three small single-family houses in different colours (ochre, mint, salmon), each with a fence and garden, plus a Plattenbau. Other examples: Amsterdam canal houses with step, bell and neck gables; Haussmann blocks including a cut-corner variant; a Viennese palais in Schönbrunn yellow and a baroque dome church; half-timbered houses; the Speicherstadt and a harbour crane; Bern arcade houses; a Budapest corner house with a Zsolnay roof; an unfinished Balkan house with rebar sticking out; Riga Art Nouveau.
- 4 bridge parts: bridge_truss_arch (centred anchor, tag overhead, see-through between members, no ground shadow), bridge_pylon, bridge_lamp and houseboat.
- Manifest entries follow the building_oldtown pattern: angle c, layers base + lights, anchor on the ground, extent_m. Tags are prop, building, city, mirror_left, plus the style and the zone (outskirts or center).
- Shared files got only small additive edits: a 5-line registry hook in props.py, and in render_all.py the new module is added to the code-hash dependencies. Cache keys of all existing sets are unchanged.

Checks:
- validate_manifest.py: 153 sets, 58.3 MB PNG, 0 errors, 1 intentional warning (bridge_pylon's near cable fan reaches below the anchor line).
- tools/run_tests.sh: 292 tests, 0 failed; integration checks OK.
- Visual checks: contact sheets and a simulated in-game street for every style and zone, by day and by night, using the game camera, edge alignment and mirroring.
- Real in-game screenshots (Warsaw day and night, Paris, Amsterdam, Vienna) came from a scratch copy of the project whose city scenery was pointed at the new sprites. The worktree's data/ and scripts/ were not touched.
deviations: Resolution is below the existing city buildings: about 9–16 px/m for centre buildings and 15–21 px/m for outskirts houses, against about 22 px/m for the old ones. The reason is the 60 MB PNG budget. I measured that the cost is genuine detail at roughly 1 byte/px; dither, sample count, noise and brick contrast barely change it. A single factor RES_SCALE in props_cities.py rescales every building at once.

Six styles have no outskirts-specific building: german_old, belgian, paris, italian, vienna, central. Fallback suggestions are in docs/sprites.md, e.g. paris -> city_french_maison, vienna/central/german_old -> city_german_house.
The Gebäudeliste is documented in docs/sprites.md (section 'Städte: regionale Gebäude und Brückenbauteile'), not in docs/staedte.md, to avoid merge conflicts.

Additions not in the contract: bridge_truss_arch has a lights layer with two hanging lamps; bridge_pylon is floodlit at night. Neither the arch nor the pylon casts a ground shadow, because the renderer draws the water and deck itself.
houseboat tags are boat, water, mirror_left (not building/city). bridge_lamp tags are bridge, road, mirror_left.
notes_for_lead: Building ids by style (outskirts | center): hanse: city_hanse_crane | city_hanse_gabled, city_hanse_kontor, city_hanse_speicher. german: city_german_house, city_german_mietshaus | city_german_gruenderzeit, city_german_office. german_old: – | city_german_old_fachwerk, city_german_old_fachwerk_b, city_german_old_barock. dutch: city_dutch_terrace | city_dutch_canal, city_dutch_canal_b. belgian: – | city_belgian_terrace, city_belgian_stone. paris: – | city_paris_haussmann, city_paris_corner. french: city_french_maison, city_french_sud | city_french_immeuble. spanish: city_spanish_casa | city_spanish_block, city_spanish_ladrillo. italian: – | city_italian_palazzo, city_italian_block, city_italian_venezia. vienna: – | city_vienna_palais, city_vienna_kirche, city_vienna_zinshaus. swiss: city_swiss_chalet | city_swiss_laube. central: – | city_central_barock, city_central_jugendstil, city_central_eckturm. eastern: city_eastern_house_a, city_eastern_house_b, city_eastern_house_c | city_eastern_plattenbau. balkan: city_balkan_house, city_balkan_house_b | city_balkan_church, city_balkan_plattenbau. baltic: city_baltic_wood, city_baltic_wood_b | city_baltic_jugendstil. All ids carry the props/ prefix. The contract's country style 'austrian' should use the vienna sets.

PNG budget is tight: these 50 sets add 5.95 MB, bringing the total to 58.3 of validate_manifest's 60 MB. The landmarks will probably push it past 60. Options: raise --max-mb in validate_manifest.py to about 64–66, or set RES_SCALE = 0.85 in props_cities.py and re-render with `render_all.py --only props/city_` (saves about 1.6 MB; ~25 min with CE_THREADS=2 on the busy machine). Lossless GPU memory if all 50 are loaded is 48.7 MB; a stage only needs its target city's style.

Placement: buildings use the same rules as the existing city props (align: edge, extent_m, mirror_left). The anchor is the centre of the front face on the ground, rendered for the right roadside; the road-facing left wall is fully detailed. city_hanse_crane is a one-off harbour object, so give it a low chance.
bridge_truss_arch: cell centred on the carriageway centre. Clear width 29.4 m (posts at ±14.7 m inner, ±15.9 m outer), crown height 15.6 m, repeat every ~40 m. Use scale for other road widths.

bridge_pylon: anchor is the pylon foot at deck level on the right roadside. Leg 82 m plus a 6 m tip; it leans slightly toward the road. Rendered at a 3/4 view (yaw −20°). The forward cable fan extends ~33 m left (toward the road) and the rear fan ~25 m right, with ends down to 7 m below the anchor line. Place it at the anchor, not edge-aligned, about 3 m outside the railing.

bridge_lamp is a 4.85 m candelabra with three lanterns; anchor at its foot; place every 25–30 m on the railing line. houseboat is 16 × 4.6 m; anchor at the waterline under the middle of the side facing the road; edge-align it on the water.

Merge: props.py (registry hook after CATCHER) and render_all.py (CODE['prop'] and the deps dict in code_hash) are small additive edits; if the landmarks agent edits the same lines, keep both. manifest.json only gained new entries; all 103 existing entries are byte-identical. The render cache is per worktree, so merge the manifests as a JSON union rather than re-rendering.

Review artefacts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/cities/buildings/ under contact/ (overview_buildings.png, overview_bridges.png), streets/ (street_<style>_<zone>.jpg, the bridge scenes, streets_overview.jpg) and shots/ (in-game screenshots; ingame_grid.jpg combines Paris, Amsterdam, Vienna and Warsaw).
